json_library.scope: Pinned JSON parser/writer; files, pointer/patch utilities, incremental reader and non-standard syntax disabled; bounded nesting and owner allocator required

scope: Production ARM64 pinned parser/writer, owner allocator, document/transfer/publication code and four complete NRO probes. Independent Python JSON/type/byte models; OS, RO, filesystem and outer game scheduling are modeled. No physical timing, full-stack or durability guarantee.
acceptance_limits: JSON and output operations are synchronous; 64-level nesting and individual frame reports do not establish a full stack or physical timing bound
Per-document/buffer requested-memory limits include allocator state and overlapping replacements, excluding outer objects, input and arena/metadata overhead
Mutable pools retain replaced/unpublished nodes and strings until reset; raw mutable APIs require checked library contracts and valid ownership
Duplicate keys can be retained; application schemas and uniqueness remain caller policy
Exact 64-bit integers are supported within range; larger numbers may round to double or fail; no arbitrary precision
The output size cap is checked after memory-bounded candidate serialization
Cooperative loading retains prior data on failure but does not provide a snapshot under same-size concurrent file changes
Publication is backup-preserving and explicitly restored in the probe; interrupted mutations need inspection and explicit recovery
The unchanged pending kernel and all four probes require one combined physical Batch 8 acceptance
Full Menyoo, hosted STL, global constructors, static-local and exception policies remain separate work
harness_corrections: Corrected test expectations to the authored Parse/Write enum values; runtime depth refusal was already functioning
Used a 128-byte file-parse budget to force admission refusal; a tiny input can legitimately fit 256 bytes
